name: Mercy Pengelly
languages: Spanish (from a girlhood in the Cornish mines at Real del Monte, Mexico)
equipment: A black stuff dress, a black shawl and a straw bonnet with a black ribbon, and stout miner's boots under all of it
Navy revolver (her late husband Jacob's, a Colt 1851), 6 loaded, which she cleans every Saturday and has never fired at a man
Pick handle, from the claim, which she uses as a walking stick
A Wesleyan hymnbook and a Bible with her family births and deaths written in the front
The deed to the Jacob Pengelly claim on Shadow Gulch, worked out, and a sack of the last ore from it
A basket: bread, saffron buns, a jar of tea, bandages and a bottle of liniment
The key to the Bible Christian chapel on Cornish Row, where she preaches on Sunday evenings
features: Two Tongues (Immigrant origin: she speaks English and Spanish fluently; she has advantage on Insight and Perception to follow a conversation the speakers think she cannot understand, and among the Cornish of the basin, and among Mexican and Hispano workers, she is trusted one step sooner than an outsider)

Fire and Brimstone (Preacher, using WIS: as an action she preaches. Steady: allies within 30 ft who hear her gain 1d6 + WIS temporary hit points and end frightened and Shaken. Shake: enemies within 30 ft make a WIS save, DC 8 + proficiency + WIS, or are frightened of her until the end of her next turn. Uses equal to her WIS modifier per short rest. No miracles: only words, and people believing them)

Comfort the Afflicted (Preacher: she stabilizes a dying creature as a bonus action with a DC 10 Medicine check, and it regains 1 hit point; once per long rest, ten minutes with someone grieving, frightened or ashamed ends their Shaken condition and tells her what truly troubles them)

The Flock (Preacher, 2nd level: wherever there is a church or a gathering of decent people she finds shelter, a meal, news and someone to speak for her; once per town, an hour's preaching gives the party +1 Reputation there, or −1 to someone she preaches against by name)

Calling: Shepherd (Preacher, 3rd level: Steady also gives each ally advantage on its next attack roll or saving throw before the end of its next turn, and Comfort the Afflicted can be used once per short rest)
Ability Score Improvement (Preacher, 4th level: +1 Wisdom, +1 Charisma)
Color in the Creek (Prospector background: she worked Jacob's claim beside him and can read rock and ore; every claim-owner on Shadow Gulch talks to her)

personality.traits: I am plain-spoken and I feed everybody. I quote Scripture at length and I do not apologise for it. I laugh loudly, and I have been known to slap a man.
personality.ideals: Every soul is worth the same to God, and a mine owner's is not worth more because it has a bigger house.
personality.bonds: My Jacob, killed in the Lodestar in February when a stope came down that Cap'n Rosevear said was safe. The Cornish women of Cornish Row, who have no one else to speak for them. My son Tom, nine, who wants to go underground.
personality.flaws: I keep promises even when I should not. Hender Rosevear told me a thing in chapel and made me swear, and I have sworn, and it is eating me.

appearance: A tall, raw-boned Cornishwoman of thirty-eight with a weathered red face, strong grey eyes, greying fair hair under a black bonnet, and a voice that carries the length of a mine drift without trying. She wears mourning and walks with the pick handle like a bishop with his crook.
backstory: Mercy Pengelly was born in Cornwall and taken as a child to the Cornish silver mines at Real del Monte in Mexico, where her father was a mine captain, and grew up speaking Spanish to her friends and Cornish English at home. She married Jacob Pengelly at nineteen and followed the mines with him to Grass Valley, Virginia City and finally Argent. When Jacob was killed underground at the Lodestar in February, Aurelius Stannard paid for the funeral and gave her $200 and his sympathy. She has buried her grief in work: she nurses, preaches at the little Bible Christian chapel on Cornish Row, feeds half the tracklayers, and argues with the Miners' Union about the Chinese. She knows more about who is drinking, who is in debt and who is frightened in Argent than anyone but the bartender at the Silver Dollar.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Mercy is the camp's conscience and its best informant. She gives the party a way into the Cornish miners, the boarding houses and the women of the camp, and in sl-scenario-002 she is the person who can stand in front of the mob at the Cut and make it listen. Her arc is her promise: Cap'n Hender Rosevear, the Lodestar's mine captain, told her in chapel in August that the Lodestar is worked out: its main vein pinched out in January, and Jacob died in February in a stope Stannard ordered opened to find it again against Rosevear's advice. She swore to tell no one. She will keep the promise until a player gives her a reason that outweighs it (a life at stake, or Erasmus Ashworth's murder), and then she will take the party to Rosevear herself (Clue C2).
dmNotes.voice: Strong West Cornish: my lover, my handsome, dreckly (later), proper job, where to? for where is it? She drops into Spanish to swear. When she preaches she sounds like a different woman, slower and enormous.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: keep her people fed and safe, and stop anyone else dying for the Lodestar. Secondary: see justice for Jacob, which she has not admitted to herself is what she wants. Tertiary: keep her son out of the mine.
dmNotes.secrets: Rosevear's confession (C2). And something she has not connected: in July Obed Becket asked her whether she wanted to sell the last ore from Jacob's claim to the Lodestar mill at twice the market price, and she refused out of pride. Others did not (Clue C4: the Lodestar is buying ore from small claims to make its bars).
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: hospitable, immediately, and frank. Toward Phoebe Lanyon: a fellow Cornish daughter; they argue happily about tea. Toward Llew Treharne: she likes him and thinks he is a fool about Stannard. Toward Stannard: grateful, and uneasy about being grateful. Toward Ong Pak-wai and his crew: she brings them bread, which the Miners' Union has not forgiven. Toward Bridget Cahill: a rivalry over who feeds the tracklayers better, and deep respect.
